raised.note: confirmed by two sources in the run; the URLs were not saved
raised.value: €17.5M from the European Innovation Council Accelerator, plus a separate $21M contract from the European Space Agency

team_size.value: over 100, including more than 30 PhD holders

entry.idea: MBRYONICS designs and builds the optical hardware, like laser communication terminals, that let satellites send data to each other and to ground stations using light instead of radio.
entry.lesson: Owning the entire technical stack, from hardware to software, in a specialised deep-tech niche can make a small company the default supplier once demand for that niche takes off.
entry.name: MBRYONICS

growth.reason: It is creating 125 new jobs and building a second large manufacturing facility to reach thousands of terminals per year, backed by a major EU grant and an ESA contract.

market.reason: Satellite operators worldwide need higher-capacity communication links as the number of satellites in orbit keeps growing, a large and expanding space infrastructure market.

tech.reason: Designing and fabricating photonic hardware for space, including optical terminals and quantum key distribution, is deep, patent-protected engineering that takes years to replicate.

sources.title: Galway-based Mbryonics bags €17.5m from European accelerator

entry.twist: It builds a full vertical stack itself, from ground-based optics to satellite payloads to the network software that runs them, rather than supplying just one piece of the puzzle.
entry.who_pays: Space agencies and satellite communications companies pay for MBRYONICS' optical terminals, ground systems and related engineering services.
entry.why_now: The number of satellites in orbit is growing fast, and radio-based communication is running out of capacity, making optical links a necessary upgrade for satellite operators.
